sources.citation: Kosaka, Ryuichi. 2000. A Descriptive Study of the Lachi Language: syntactic description, historical reconstruction and genetic relation. PhD thesis, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. https://tufs.repo.nii.ac.jp/records/1164

sources.note: Describes Long-haired Lachi (Tan Loi hamlet < Ban Phung) = lach1248, NOT White Lachi: Intro p.1 says the Ban Pang / Ban May (White Lachi) villages 'seem to have already abandoned their mother tongue and came to speak Nung'; ch.6.3 (pp.131-136) uses only Lachi (K) and Jinchang (LJC), no Ban Pang data. Its stress remarks (ch.1 pp.7-9, 23, 28: phrase/word-final 'major' syllable carries full stress and tone, preceding minor syllables reduced; 'stress-placing tendency is of rear-ward nature') therefore apply to lach1248 only.

Defines Central Lachi = Ban Pang = White Lachi; notes only Robert 1913 and a few forms from Edmondson & Nguyen Van Loi 1997 exist for Ban Pang, and that Vietnamese scholars' Ban Pang material 'has remained largely unavailable in published form'; gives 7 Ban Pang forms with tone numbers (comparative use only).

sources.citation: Robert, [M.] 1913. Notice sur les Lati. Revue d'ethnographie et de sociologie 4 (no. 9-12): 338-352. Paris: Leroux. (Glottolog: 'Robert, M. 1916'; Ostapirat 2000 cites 'Robert, J. 1913'.) archive.org item revuedethnogr49121913pari.

sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.343 'Langue': transcription of Lati words uses French values plus quoc-ngu tone accents; 'les tons ne semblent pas bien fixes et varient pour certains mots d'un individu a l'autre'; vocabulary (pp.344-349) was 'pris a Man P'ang' (= Ban Pang, White Lachi) with a Ban Phung column; brief syntax notes. The only first-hand prosodic remark on the White Lachi variety.
